public_rationale: The 16 August 2022 SayCan paper identifies a limitation in handling negation inherited from its language models, while reporting improvements with chain-of-thought prompting [e1]. A May 2022 study found GPT-3 performed mostly at chance on psycholinguistic tasks probing implied meanings [e2]. Together, these findings support the claim that contemporary models had material weaknesses in interpreting intended meaning [e1, e2]. SayCan also demonstrated successful request interpretation and reported 84% planning success across 101 tasks, but that aggregate measure does not isolate understanding or establish near-perfect interpretation [e3].
limitations: The evaluations do not provide a representative accuracy rate for understanding everyday user intentions or cover every contemporary model.
Planning and execution failures cannot all be counted as misunderstandings.
The evidence does not establish a permanent limitation; SayCan reported improvements with prompting [e1].

statement.excerpt: And we know from all the research on large language models that they simply aren’t reliable enough to give us anything like 100% clarity on user intentions.
statement.document_title: What’s wrong with Google’s new robot project

from_speaker: anything like 100% clarity on user intentions
our_interpretation: This describes models available when the post appeared, not all future models.
The plain reading is that contemporary models made recurring, material mistakes interpreting requests and intended meanings.
Use the current research year, 2022-01-01 through 2022-08-18, for this ongoing observation. Research evaluations have no standard quarterly reporting period.
Physical execution failures, factual errors and harmful compliance alone do not establish misunderstanding.
criteria.support_condition: Contemporary evaluations show recurring errors interpreting requests or implied meanings, materially short of near-perfect reliability across varied inputs.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Broad contemporary evaluations establish near-perfect interpretation of varied requests, including implied meanings and ambiguous references, without material recurring misunderstandings.

evidence.explanation: Tests of presuppositions and implied meanings found substantial weaknesses in GPT-3, corroborating the interpretation failures in SayCan. These are controlled linguistic probes using model probabilities, not a direct estimate of misunderstanding rates in everyday user conversations.

evidence.publisher: Robotics at Google and Everyday Robots
evidence.explanation: The project reports 84% planning success across 101 tasks and demonstrates correctly distinguishing a request for cleanup from one for a replacement drink. This qualifies the criticism: models often interpreted requests successfully, although aggregate planning success is not a pure measure of understanding.
